title: SpaceX won’t remove all of xAI’s unpermitted turbines for another year
slides: Why would SpaceX tolerate unpermitted turbines for twelve more months?
State regulators demanded removal, yet approval delays persist
Inspection found four turbines operating without required environmental permits
Your project's compliance timeline just became much more unpredictable
Audit your own permits immediately; don't assume enforcement deadlines.
thread_text:
1. Why tolerate violations?

SpaceX’s turbines run unpermitted for 12 more months—approval delays don’t erase the violation. Regulators ordered removal, yet the clock keeps ticking.

2. Approval delay, not grace

State regulators demanded removal, but the permit process stalled—so enforcement waits. Delays become de facto extensions, setting a risky precedent.

3. Four turbines, no permits

An inspection found four turbines operating without required environmental permits. The operators knew, yet continued running—until the state stepped in.

4. Your compliance just got harder

This case signals that enforcement timelines can stretch unpredictably. Your project’s compliance calendar is now less certain—expect delays or sudden crackdowns.

5. Audit your permits now

Don’t assume deadlines hold. Run a prompt on ChatGPT to list your permits and expiration dates—if you haven’t, start there. Ignorance won’t shield you.
